sentences.text:
This is a reference u/s 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as L.A.
Act).
The land of village Pansali came under Government acquisition and an Award No.04/2011-12 was passed.
The dispute that has been referred on 13.02.2012, was pertaining to apportionment of the compensation of land of khasra no.11//4/2 (1-00).
The dispute was between aforesaid 7 Interested Persons (hereinafter referred to as IPs).

LAC also remitted an amount of Rs.16,66,209/-
being compensation of acquired land.
2. Notice of the reference was issued to the IPs.
However, only IP No.1 & IP no.7 came forward and filed their respective claims.

CLAIMS 3. Claim of IP-1 Sh. Sanjeev Malhotra:- IP-1 has claimed that he had purchased the aforesaid land from Sh. Dhan Singh who was attorney of Sh. Om Prakash, Zile Singh and Satbir all s/o late Sh.
Jodha r/o Village & Post Office Pehladpur Banger, Delhi.
The said land was purchased vide duly registered sale-deed dated 18.10.1988 and mutation was sanctioned in favour of IP-1/claimant vide order dated 27.10.1997.
IP-1 has further claimed that he was in possession of land in question since its purchase till its acquisition.

The said land has been acquired by government vide aforesaid Award and IP-1 is entitled to receive entire compensation w.r.t. land measuring 1 bigha out of khasra no.11/4/2 situated in the Revenue Estate of Village Pansali.

4. Claim of IP No.7 Sh. Anil Luthra:- IP no.7 has claimed that he was the owner and was in possession of agricultural land measuring 1 bigha in khasra no.11//4/2 situated in the Revenue Estate of Village Pansali.
The said land was purchased by him from Sh. Dhan Singh i.e. GPA holder of Om Prakash, Zile Singh and Satbir all s/o late Sh. Jodha.
The said land was purchased by virtue of registered sale-deed dated 18.10.1988.
The IP No.7 has further claimed that he was in continuous possession of said land since the day of its purchase by him till the same was acquired by government.
Hence, IP-7 is entitled to receive entire compensation qua said land.
5. It is pertinent to mention that notice of present petition was duly served upon IP-2 to 6.
Inspite of service IP-2 to 6 failed to file their respective claims.
Consequently, IP-2 to 6 were proceeded exparte vide order dated 16.10.2012.

Issues:-
6. On completion of pleadings following issues were framed on 17.01.2013:-
1. Which of the IPs is entitled to receive the compensation and if so to what amount?
2. Relief.
Evidence:-

2 7. In support of his claim IP-1 produced and examined the following witness and has also relied upon following documents:-
IP1W-1
Sh . Sanjeev Malhotra/IP-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.IP1W-1/A and relied upon document Ex.IP1W-1/1 i.e. sale-deed dated 18.10.1988.

IP1W-2 Sh. Sunil Kumar, Patwari brought the summoned record i.e. khatoni for the year 2003-04 of village Pansali w.r.t. land comprising khasra no.11//4 /2 min(1-00)
and proved the same as Ex.IP1W-2/1.
IP1W-3

Sh. Anup Singh ,Record Keeper, from office of Sub-Registrar II, Kashmiri Gate, Delhi proved sale-deed dated 18.10.1998 i.e. Ex.IP1W-1/1.
IP1W-4 Sh. Satish Kumar, Clerk from Sub-Registrar Office, Gurgaon proved the registered GPA dated 06.10.1988 i.e. IP1W-4/1.
IP1W-5 Sh. Chhatarpal Singh, Kanoongo, from DM Office, North, Alipur proved khatoni for the year 1988-89 of village Pansali in respect of the khasra no.11//4/2 min (1-00), khata no.46/11 i.e.
Ex.IP1W-5/1 and khasra girdawari for the year 1993-2003 i.e. Ex. IP1W-5/2.
8.

In support of his claim IP-7 produced and examined the following witness and has also relied upon following documents:-
IP7W-1
Sh. Anil Luthra tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.IP7W-1/A and relied upon document Ex.IP7W-1/1 i.e. sale-deed and photocopy of the registered GPA dated 06.10.1988 Mark A. IP7W-2

Sh. Hira Lal, Preservation Assistant,
Department of Delhi Archives proved the sale-deed dated 18.10.1988 executed by Sh.
Dhan Singh in favour of Anil Luthra i.e. Ex. IP7W-2/1.
IP7W-3 Sh. Dhan Singh, deposed that he was attorney holder of Sh. Om Prakash, Zile Singh and Satbir sons of Sh. Jodha, in respect of land situated at Village Pansali.
The total land was measuring 5 acres.
The land bearing khasra no.11//4/2 was part of that 5 acres of land.
Sh. Dhan Singh further deposed that he was attorney holder of the total area measuring 02 Bigha 15 Biswas comprising in khasra no.11//4/2.

IP7W3 deposed that he had sold one Bigha of land falling in khasra no.11//4/2 to Anil Luthra and one Bigha of land falling in said khasra to Sanjeev Malhotra and had also handed over possession of said land to them.
IP7W3 i.e. Sh. Dhan Singh admitted/ proved the sale-deed executed by him in favour of IPs Sanjeev Malhotra as well as in favour of IP-7/ Anil Malhotra.

Thus IP7W3 i.e. Sh. Dhan Singh has supported the claim of IP-1/Sanjeev Malhotra as well as IP No.7/
Anil Luthra.
9. I have heard the arguments advanced by Sh. M.C. Verma, Ld. Counsel for IP No.1 and Sh.Vineet Rana, ld. Counsel for IP No.7.
I have perused the record carefully.
I have also perused the written arguments filed on behalf of IP o.1 as well as IP No.7.

sentences.text: As per reference u/s 30-31 of LA Act forwarded to this Court by LAC IP No.1 Sanjeev Malhotra is one of the recorded owner qua land in question and IP No.7 Anil Luthra is also claiming ownership qua land in question.
Hence, there is title dispute between parties.
11. Perusal of claim filed by IP No.1 as well as IP No.7 shows that their claims are identical.
Both IP's i.e. IP No.1 and IP No.7 have claimed that they had purchased 1 Bigha of land each falling in khasra no.11//4/2 situated in revenue estate of village Pansali from Sh. Dhan Singh.
Both had purchased said land vide Registered sale-deed dated 18.10.1988.
Both ave claimed that Sh. Dhan Singh was GPA holder of Sh. Om Prakash, Zile Singh and Satbir all s/o late Sh. Jodha.
Both have claimed that they were in possession of land purchased by them since the date of its purchase till the same was acquired by Government.
Both have claimed that Sh. Dhan Singh was GPA holder in respect of land measuring 2 Bigha and 15 Biswas of khasra no.11//4/2.
Both have claimed that they had purchased different plot of land.

12. Perusal of record further shows that IPNo.7 in his written arguments/ submissions has stated/written as under:-
"6.

That it is admitted fact on behalf of both the IP's that they both purchased their different plot of land i.e. 1 Bigha each from Dr. Dhan Singh who was the Attorney of registered owner (namely Sh. Om Prakash, Zilley Singh and Satbir all sons of late Sh.
Jodha, all r/o Villae Prahladpur Bangar, Delhi) in respect of land measuring 2 bigha and 15 biswas out of khasra no.11/4/2.
7.

That Dr. Dhan Singh was also examined as IP7W3 on 11.03.2020 wherein has admitted the Sale deed in favou of IP No.7 exhibited as Ex.IP-7W2/1 as well as GPA which was in his favour having right of 02 Bigha 15 Biswa out of khasra n.11/4/2.

In fact, the admitted case of both the parties is that Sh. Om Prakash etc. were owner of 2 bigha 15 biswas out of khasra no.11/4/2 on 18.10.1988 when both the sale deeds measuring 1 bigha each totaling 2 bigha was executed by Dhan Singh being attorney.

Since, area of both the sale-deeds has not been demarcated out of 2 bigha and 15 bisws, therefore, IP No.1& 7 are co-owner I respect of each part of khasra no.11/4/2 and hence if 1 bigha land is acquired, both the recorded owners are entitled to get equal compensation.
8.

That the aforesaid land i.e. 01 Bigha 00 Biswa out of Kh. no.11/4/2 was got acquired vide Award No.04/2011- 2012 L.A.C. (North/West), Kanjhawala in respect of the aforesaid agricultural land, therefore the IP No.7 also got the right of half of the compensation/ claim amount.
Hence, the claim of IP No.7 may be released in favour of the IP No.7.

Prayer:
In view of the above submissions, it is, therefore, most humbly prayed that the compensation/claim amount may be awarded in favour of IP No.1 & 7 equally i.e. half Union Of India vs Sh. Sanjeev Malhotra on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45479939/
4 and half, in the interest of justice".

Similarly IP No.1 in his written arguments/ submissions has stated/ written as under:-
"6.

That it is admitted fact on behalf of both the IP's that they both purchased their different plot of land i.e. 1 Bigha each from Dr. Dhan Singh who was the Attorney of registered owner (namely Sh. Om Prakash, Zilley Singh and Sh.Satbir all sons of Sh.
Jodha, all r/o Village Prahladpur Bangar, Delhi) in respect of land measuring 2 bigha and 15 biswas out of khasra no.11/4/2.
7.

That Dr. Dhan Singh was also examined as IP-1W3 on 11.03.2020 wherein he has admitted the Sale Deed in favour of IP No.1 exhibited as Ex.IP-1W3/1 as well as GPA which was in his favour having right of 02 Bigha 15 Biswas out of Khasra no.11/4/2.

In fact, the admitted case of boh the parties is that Sh. Om Prakash etc. were owner of 2 bigha 15 biswas out of khasra no.11/4/2 on 18.10.1988 when both the sale-deeds measuring 1 bigha each totaling 2 bigha was executed by Dhan Singh being attorney.

Since, area of both sale-deeds has not been demarcated out of 2 bigha and 15 biswas,
therefore, IP No.1&7 are co-owner in respect of each part of khasra no.11/4/2 and hence if 01 bigha land is acquired, both the recorded owners are entitled to get equal compensation".
13.

Keeping in view the aforesaid facts, circumstances and discussion made hereinabove I am of the considered view that both IP's i.e. IP No.1/Sanjeev Malhotra & IP No.7/Anil Luthra are entitled to receive/get equal share i.e. half share each of the compensation amount deposited by LAC in Court.
Both issues are decided accordingly.
14. The reference petition is answered.

15. District Nazir is directed to remit/distribute the awarded amount of the land to the entitled IPs in above terms subject to filing of necessary documents, completion of necessary formalities and after receiving the amount from concerned Bank.
16.
Copy of this judgement be sent to the LAC.
17. File be consigned to record-room after necessary Digitally signed by compliance.
